# AP-INC-002 Operational Incident Response and Review

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This policy establishes the procedures for the timely reporting, coordination, and review of all operational incidents at AeroPolicy Airport. It ensures that incidents are managed in a manner that prioritizes safety, compliance, and continuous improvement. The scope of this policy encompasses all incidents that occur on the airport premises, including but not limited to those involving baggage, restricted items, ramp safety, and equipment. These incidents may affect operational efficiency, passenger safety, or regulatory compliance. The procedures outlined in this policy apply to all staff members, contractors, and third-party vendors who are involved in the operation of the airport.

Operational incidents may arise from a variety of sources, including equipment malfunctions, human error, or environmental factors. The response to these incidents must be coordinated across departments to ensure that all relevant parties are informed and that corrective actions are implemented promptly. This policy also outlines the roles and responsibilities of key personnel, including the Reporting Staff Member, Incident Coordinator, and Airside Duty Manager, to ensure a structured and effective incident management process.

The purpose of this policy is to provide a clear framework for incident reporting, to facilitate a timely and coordinated response, and to ensure that all incidents are reviewed for root causes and corrective actions. By following these procedures, AeroPolicy Airport aims to maintain a high standard of operational safety and service quality.

## 2. Incident Categories

Operational incidents at AeroPolicy Airport are categorized into four main types: baggage incidents, restricted-item incidents, ramp safety incidents, and equipment incidents. Each category has specific characteristics and potential impacts on airport operations. Baggage incidents involve the misplacement, damage, or delay of luggage and may affect passenger satisfaction and operational efficiency. Restricted-item incidents involve the discovery or mishandling of items that are prohibited or restricted by airport security regulations. Ramp safety incidents refer to any event that poses a risk to personnel or aircraft on the ramp area, such as unsecured equipment or hazardous material exposure. Equipment incidents involve malfunctions or failures of airport equipment, including ground support equipment, baggage handling systems, or communication devices.

Each incident type requires a different level of attention and response, depending on its potential impact and the regulatory requirements it may trigger. For example, baggage incidents must be escalated in accordance with the procedures outlined in AP-BAG-001, while restricted-item incidents must be reported and managed in compliance with AP-SEC-003. The categorization of incidents ensures that appropriate resources and expertise are allocated to address each situation effectively. This classification also supports the post-incident review process by providing a structured framework for analyzing the causes and implementing corrective measures.

## 3. Reporting and First Response

All operational incidents must be reported immediately by the staff member who first identifies or becomes aware of the incident. The reporting staff member is responsible for providing a clear and accurate description of the incident, including the location, time, and any immediate effects. This information should be relayed to the Airside Duty Manager or the Incident Coordinator, depending on the nature and severity of the incident. The first response to an incident should focus on ensuring the safety of personnel and the public, mitigating any immediate risks, and preventing further escalation.

The Airside Duty Manager is responsible for assessing the initial impact of the incident and determining the appropriate level of response. In cases where an incident involves a potential safety hazard or regulatory violation, the Airside Duty Manager must initiate the coordination process with the Incident Coordinator. The Incident Coordinator is tasked with ensuring that all relevant departments are informed and that the incident is logged and managed according to established procedures. The first response should also include any necessary containment measures, such as securing the area, isolating affected equipment, or evacuating personnel if required.

## 4. Incident Coordinator Duties

The Incident Coordinator is responsible for overseeing the entire incident management process, from initial reporting to post-incident review. The Incident Coordinator must open an incident record for every reported incident before the end of the shift in which it was reported. This record should include all relevant details, such as the nature of the incident, the time and location, and any immediate actions taken. The Incident Coordinator must also ensure that all affected departments are informed and that the incident is escalated to the appropriate level if necessary.

The Incident Coordinator is responsible for coordinating the response efforts across different departments and ensuring that all required actions are carried out in a timely and efficient manner. This includes facilitating communication between the reporting staff member, the Airside Duty Manager, and any other relevant personnel. The Incident Coordinator must also monitor the progress of the incident response and make adjustments as needed to ensure that the incident is resolved effectively. The role of the Incident Coordinator is critical in maintaining operational continuity and ensuring that all incidents are managed in a manner that prioritizes safety and compliance.

## 5. Post-Incident Review

Following the resolution of an operational incident, a post-incident review must be conducted to determine the root cause and identify corrective actions. This review is led by the Incident Coordinator in collaboration with the relevant departments and may involve a multidisciplinary team to ensure a comprehensive analysis. The review process should include a detailed examination of the incident, including the sequence of events, the actions taken, and the outcomes. This analysis should be documented in a formal report that is reviewed by the Airside Duty Manager and other senior management personnel.

The post-incident review must also assess the effectiveness of the response and identify any gaps in the incident management process. This includes evaluating whether the incident was reported and managed in accordance with established procedures and whether the corrective actions proposed are sufficient to prevent recurrence. The findings of the review should be used to update existing policies, procedures, and training programs to enhance operational safety and efficiency. The review process is an essential component of continuous improvement and ensures that AeroPolicy Airport maintains a high standard of operational excellence.

## 6. Records

All incident records must be maintained in a secure and accessible manner, with detailed information on the incident, the response, and the corrective actions taken. These records should be retained for the duration required by regulatory authorities and internal audit procedures. The Incident Coordinator is responsible for ensuring that all records are properly documented, stored, and made available for review when necessary. Access to incident records should be restricted to authorized personnel only, and all records must be protected against unauthorized modification or disclosure. Regular audits of incident records may be conducted to ensure compliance with this policy and to identify any areas for improvement in the incident management process.
